review: The whole hymn is Psalm 119: 1:1–2 is v.9 almost word for word (בַּמֶּה יְזַכֶּה־נַּעַר אֶת־אָרְחוֹ), 1:3–4 vv.1–3, 2:1 v.10 (בְּכָל־לִבִּי דְרַשְׁתִּיךָ), 2:3 v.35 (הַדְרִיכֵנִי בִּנְתִיב מִצְוֺתֶיךָ), 3:1–3 v.11 (בְּלִבִּי צָפַנְתִּי אִמְרָתֶךָ), 4:4 v.37, 5:1–4 vv.14–16 and 24, 6:1–4 vv.13–14 and 111.

1:1–2 keeps the psalm's own division: the Arabic puts 'his ways' in line 1 and 'the young man' in line 2, and so does v.9, where נַעַר stands after the verb; the Hebrew therefore does not move the subject up into the first line, even though that would read more smoothly.

3:4 לְךָ, אֲדֹנִי — the Arabic إِلَيْكَ يَا رَبِّي is the tail of 'lest I sin against You'; the Hebrew leaves the prepositional phrase as its own short line, exactly as the print does, so the stanza ends on the address rather than on the verb.

5:3–4 וּבְמִצְוֺתָיו אֶשְׁעָה — the Arabic وَبِوَصَايَاهُ أَنَا أَلْهَجُ splits 'I' from 'meditate'; the Hebrew puts the pronoun into the verb and uses שָׁעָה ('to gaze, to regard', Isa 17:7) for the first clause and הָגָה (Ps 1:2) for the second, so the two verbs of the psalm's delight are both present.

6:1 בִּשְׂפָתַי סִפַּרְתִּים — the Arabic وَبِفَمِي حَسَبْتُهָה is 'with my mouth I recounted them', which is v.13 (בִּשְׂפָתַי סִפַּרְתִּי); the Hebrew keeps the psalm's lips rather than the Arabic's mouth, since the verse is being quoted.
